title: E. Relationship correctness
definition: Required relationships exist between the right endpoints, in the right direction, with the right type and a label wherever the label carries meaning. Inferred relationships are marked as such; unsupported connections are absent.
questions: Are inferred relationships distinguished from source-explicit facts?

severity.critical: A dependency reversed; a required architecture edge missing or unlabeled; a calls/reads/writes type swapped; an inferred link presented as fact.
severity.major: A sequence edge missing; a label that is vague ('relates').

deterministic: relationship_present (direction, type, required label, label terms)
relationship_absent for reversed or forbidden edges
model_judge: 'Does every arrow say something true that the source supports?'
human: Reviewer checks every inferred relationship's justification

passCriteria: All critical relationship assertions pass on every run. An unlabeled arrow never counts as an architecture relationship where the label is needed.
failCriteria: Any reversed dependency, missing required edge, or unlabeled architecture edge.
passExample: 'Retrieval service —reads passages→ Vector store'; 'Orchestrator —writes answer + citations→ Answer log'.
failExample: 'Vector store → Retrieval service' with no label; 'Orchestrator —reads→ Answer log'.

judgeScale.meaning: Many wrong, reversed or unlabeled edges.
Required edges present; one vague label or one questionable inference unmarked.
Every edge correct, directed, typed and labelled; inferences marked.
